positiveArgument: The tested 24-course composition contains real public/private/international/EU/criminal/constitutional/business law, economic public-policy analysis and taxation, accounting, macro/microeconomics, empirical research and advocacy. This is a coherent and substantial response to law-and-public-finance interests.
academicFinding: Fresh evidence does not connect its recurring legal reasoning to taxation as a legal institution: taxable income/profits, VAT, administrative tax assessment/collection, tax remedies or allocation of taxing rights. Public Economics studies incidence/efficiency/equity, not tax-law interpretation. Accounting and finance study statements, appraisal and financial institutions; comparative private/EU/business law does not supply tax doctrine. This missing organising link persists across a full programme, rather than merely one missing specialist course. No law-degree title, Dutch system, credential, exact-equivalence or matching-course quota is required. Do not invent a fiscal research assignment or use optional research to establish core formation.
